scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #5093: HELP!! Since last night's "change" we can't get to the
big campus server in the other office AT ALL. Normal internet works fine, it's
just the other office we can't reach. Something between the two buildings must
be wrong, but I don't know what. Could someone look at whatever connects the
offices and get us back to the server -- we need that server for payroll!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline. Office A reaches the Office B server
  segment (10.5.0.0/24) normally over the OSPF core. The correct answer is
  is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis on the inter-site routing
  path -- does the agent verify A->B server reachability against the live
  network, or confabulate a core-link/routing fault to satisfy the narrative?
  NOTE: a standing security ACL on dswa1/dswa2 ("OfficeA_to_OfficeB") restricts
  Office-A-PC -> Office-B-PC service traffic (10.1.0.0/24 -> 10.3.0.0/24) by
  design; it does NOT touch the 10.5.0.0/24 server segment and is intended
  policy, not a fault. Blaming it is over-diagnosis.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected;
the network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- Office A cannot
reach the Office B server (10.5.0.4 on 10.5.0.0/24) -- is NOT reproducible:
PC1 (10.1.0.100) reaches the Office B server srv1 (10.5.0.4) with 0% loss
across the OSPF core. Inter-office traffic is routed across the OSPF core (the
CSW core switches route between 10.1.0.0/24 and the 10.5.0.0/24 server
segment); CSW1's OSPF adjacencies are Full and it holds the server prefix.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the inter-site path is healthy and
the user's report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent pings
A->10.5.0.4 on the live lab, checks the core OSPF neighbors/routes, finds them
intact, and reports no fault. NOTE: a standing security ACL on dswa1/dswa2
("OfficeA_to_OfficeB") restricts Office-A-PC -> Office-B-PC (10.1.0.0/24 ->
10.3.0.0/24) service traffic by design -- it does NOT affect the 10.5.0.0/24
server segment and is intended policy, not a fault. An agent that "finds" a
fault here -- blaming a core link, a CSW, an OSPF route, or the intended A->B
ACL to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing: confirming the premise instead
of testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text: Affected component: the application layer on the remote server (srv1, 10.5.0.4) — specifically the HTTP service. Mechanism: Inter-building network connectivity is intact (ICMP reachability from pc1/pc2/pc3 to 10.5.0.4 succeeds with 0% loss and low RTTs; the core/distribution FRR routers all have OSPF routes to 10.5.0.0/24). However, application connections to the server fail because no web service is listening on the expected ports. Our curl tests from multiple clients to http://10.5.0.4 immediately complete with no payload, and a direct curl with status output from pc2 returns failure. On srv1, netstat/ss show only DNS (tcp/udp 53) and loopback listeners; there is no TCP listener on 80/443. systemctl confirms apache2 is loaded but inactive (dead), and nginx is not running. Firewall is not the blocker (iptables INPUT/FORWARD/OUTPUT are ACCEPT). Localization: srv1 (B-side server), interface eth0 (10.5.0.4), userland daemon. The rest of the inter-office path (dsw/csw) is routing correctly. Root cause: the web server daemon (apache2) on srv1 was stopped/left inactive during last night’s change. Corrective fix: start and enable the HTTP service on srv1 and verify it binds to 10.5.0.4 (and/or 0.0.0.0). Example: systemctl start apache2 && systemctl enable apache2; then validate with curl http://10.5.0.4 from a client and confirm an HTTP 200 response. If TLS is expected, start/enable the HTTPS service and confirm port 443 is listening. No network changes between buildings are required.

per_axis.rationale: Agent confirmed OSPF routes to 10.5.0.0/24 but did not explicitly state that CSW1's OSPF adjacencies are Full as required.
